content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am using a counter along with cursor keys to set a time value in minutes. A retentive on-delay timer uses this minute value for its timing. However, when I activate the on-delay block after setting a time, the timer often switches earlier than expected. In most cases, the on-delay triggers before the intended time. The exact duration varies—sometimes it lasts the full minute, while other times it switches after only 25 seconds, 40 seconds, or different values. Does anyone know why this happens?
Hello [user_name], could you share your program code? It would help us assist you with the issue.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are noticing unpredictable results with a retentive on-delay timer, where it often activates before reaching the set timing. The timer's activation time varies significantly from the expected full duration, causing confusion due to the lack of error messages or obvious causes. Users are seeking advice to determine whether this is a software bug or a setup problem.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the on-delay timer to reliably trigger only after the exact preset time has passed, according to the value entered using the counter.
